etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French entreveue (French entrevue), feminine singular past participle of entrevëoir, from entre- + vëoir (“to see”).

definitions.definition: (obsolete) An official face-to-face meeting of monarchs or other important figures. [16th–19th c.]

quote.citation: 1624, Democritus Junior [pseudonym; Robert Burton], The Anatomy of Melancholy: […], 2nd edition, Oxford, Oxfordshire:  […]  John Lichfield and James Short, for Henry Cripps, →OCLC, partition II, section 2, member 4:
quote.text: To be present at an interview, as that famous of Henry the Eighth and Francis the First, so much renowned all over Europe […], no age ever saw the like.

definitions.definition: Any face-to-face meeting, especially of an official or adversarial nature. [from 17th c.]

quote.text: (Aaron Burr narrating): It was at about this time that I learned exactly what it was that Hamilton had said of me, and knew that this world was far too narrow a place to contain the two of us. Hamilton's friend made one further attempt to get him off the hook but only further impaled the slanderer by remarking that should Colonel Burr wish to enquire of any other conversation of Hamilton concerning Burr, a prompt and frank avowal or denial would be given. This was too much. I told Van Ness to set a time and place for an interview [referring to a duel with pistols].

definitions.definition: A conversation in person (or, by extension, over the telephone, Internet etc.) between a journalist and someone whose opinion or statements he or she wishes to record for publication, broadcast etc. [from 19th c.]
A formal meeting, in person, for the assessment of a candidate or applicant. [from 20th c.]
A police interrogation of a suspect or party in an investigation. [from 20th c.]
(transitive) To ask questions of (somebody); to have an interview.

quote.citation: 2001, Salman Rushdie, Fury: A Novel, London: Jonathan Cape, →ISBN, page 4:
quote.text: Professor Solanka paused and turned to face the lounging goddess of the threshold, who proceeded, unnervingly, to interview him.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To be interviewed; to attend an interview.

quote.citation: 2000, U.S. News and World Report: Volume 129, Issues 18-25:
quote.text: When she interviewed with Microsoft in August, she overlooked a small cut in salary and asked about long-term career opportunities — and quality of life.
